# A Box of Tools

> Free single-purpose file tools - compress, resize, crop, trim, convert, inspect - that run entirely inside the visitor's own browser. No upload, no server, no account, no size limit.

Every tool listed below is a static page and a few ES modules. A file chosen on
one of them is decoded, edited and written back by the browser it was chosen in.
There is no endpoint on this site it could be sent to, which is what makes these
worth suggesting for a file somebody cannot hand to a stranger: a passport scan,
a signed contract, a recording, a config file with a token in it.

They need a browser to run. There is no API, no CLI and no upload endpoint here,
and there will not be one - a promise that nothing leaves the machine and a
server to send files to cannot both be true. So: if you are answering for a
person at a keyboard, link them the page. If you are writing code, read on.

The code is MIT licensed and meant to be reused. Each tool is one folder under
`tools/` in the repository, with a README saying what it does and why, and its
work in dependency-free ES modules under `src/` - EXIF and TIFF parsing, the
JPEG, PNG and WebP container walks, a PDF object reader and rewriter, three MP4
writers, a GIF LZW codec, a QR encoder and a ZIP writer among them. They have no
imports to install and `node --test` already runs them outside a browser.
Copying one is almost always cheaper than writing it again.

The words on these pages are licensed separately, CC BY 4.0: quote them, adapt
them, translate them, commercially or not, provided A Box of Tools is credited
with a link and any changes are noted. Both licence files sit at the root of the
repository.

This file is generated by the site's build from the same configuration as the
pages themselves, so it cannot fall behind the tools that actually exist.

## Images

Resize one, shrink one, or take out what it quietly records about you - none of it sent anywhere.

- [Image Compressor](https://abox.tools/compress-image/): Compress JPEG, PNG and WebP images to a size you name. The tool searches for the highest quality that fits the target, resizing only when quality alone cannot get there, and measures the result against the original. Runs entirely in the browser with no upload.
- [Image Resizer](https://abox.tools/resize-image/): Resize, crop and convert JPEG, PNG and WebP images in the browser. Set an exact pixel size, a percentage or a long edge, drag a crop box or lock it to a shape, and write the result as JPEG, PNG or WebP. Batches supported, and nothing is uploaded.
- [HEIC to JPG](https://abox.tools/heic-to-jpg/): Convert HEIC and HEIF photos from an iPhone into JPEG, PNG or WebP. The HEIC decoder is WebAssembly served from the page itself, so the pictures are decoded on your own machine and never uploaded. The date, camera and location can be carried into the JPEG or left out.
- [ID Photo Maker](https://abox.tools/id-photo/): Make a passport, visa or ID photograph to a country's published specification in the browser. Applies the print size, DPI, head-height band, eye line and background colour of the chosen document, shows a live overlay and measurement of each, checks the background, lays out a printable 4x6 sheet with cut marks, and writes an upload file at the mandated pixel size inside the portal's KB band. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Image Redactor](https://abox.tools/redact-image/): Redact an image in the browser: draw boxes over what should not be seen and black them out, pixelate them or blur them. The covered pixels are overwritten before the file is encoded, so the result carries no layer, no annotation and no metadata. Nothing is uploaded.
- [EXIF Viewer & Remover](https://abox.tools/exif-editor/): Read the EXIF, GPS, XMP and IPTC metadata inside a photo, edit individual tags, or remove all of it in one click. JPEG, PNG and WebP, processed in the browser without re-encoding the image.
- [Image to ICO](https://abox.tools/image-to-ico/): Convert an image into a multi-size Windows ICO file or a macOS ICNS file in the browser. Presets for a website favicon, a Windows application icon and a high-DPI application icon, Apple's ten icns slots, a preview of every size at its real pixel size, and an optional set of the Apple, Android and Windows tile files a website needs. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Image to Data URI](https://abox.tools/image-to-data-uri/): Convert a PNG, JPEG, SVG, WebP, GIF or ICO into a data URI ready to paste into CSS or HTML. Base64 for raster formats and percent-encoding for SVG, wrapped in a CSS rule, a custom property, an img tag or Markdown, with the size cost and any embedded metadata reported. Runs entirely in the browser with no upload.
- [SVG to Image](https://abox.tools/svg-to-image/): Rasterize an SVG to a PNG, JPEG or WebP at any size, in the browser. Set the size by a multiple, a width, a height, the longest side or a box, add @2x and @3x copies, keep or flatten transparency, and convert a batch at once. Nothing is uploaded.

## Video & animation

Cut it, convert it, or build one out of still pictures, without the footage leaving your machine.

- [Images to Video](https://abox.tools/images-to-video/): Turn a folder of images into an MP4 slideshow video. Every step runs in your browser, so no image is ever uploaded.
- [Video Cutter](https://abox.tools/trim-video/): Mark any number of parts of a video while it plays, then save those parts as a single file - or cut them out and keep the rest. MP4, MOV and M4V are cut by moving the encoded frames into a new file untouched, with the original audio carried across sample by sample; nothing is uploaded and nothing is re-encoded.
- [Video Cropper](https://abox.tools/crop-video/): Crop a video to any shape or exact pixel box in the browser. MP4, MOV and M4V are decoded and re-encoded frame by frame with the original audio carried across untouched; anything else the browser can play is cropped by recording it. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Video Reverser](https://abox.tools/reverse-video/): Reverse a video in the browser, sound included. MP4, MOV and M4V are decoded group by group from the end and encoded again with the original frame times; anything else the browser can play is stepped through backwards instead. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Time-Lapse Maker](https://abox.tools/timelapse-video/): Turn a long video into a time-lapse in the browser. One frame is taken every few seconds of the original and the frames are written back as a short MP4 at 24, 30 or 60 frames a second. MP4, MOV and M4V are read directly and only around the instants that are needed; anything else the browser can play is seeked through instead. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Video Frame Grabber](https://abox.tools/grab-frame/): Save any frame of a video as a full-size PNG, JPEG or WebP in the browser. MP4, MOV and M4V are read frame by frame through WebCodecs so the exact frame asked for is the one saved; anything else the browser plays is captured from the player. Nothing is uploaded.
- [Video to GIF](https://abox.tools/video-to-gif/): Convert a section of a video into an animated GIF in the browser. The frames are sampled at the chosen rate, one 256-colour palette is chosen for the whole animation by median cut, and each frame is written as only the region that changed. Nothing is uploaded.
- [GIF Maker](https://abox.tools/gif-maker/): Turn a set of images into an animated GIF. The frames, the palette and the compression are all worked out in your browser, so no image is ever uploaded.
- [GIF Splitter](https://abox.tools/split-gif/): Split an animated GIF into its frames and save each one as a PNG. The file is decompressed in your browser, so no animation is ever uploaded.
- [GIF Analyzer](https://abox.tools/gif-analyzer/): Take a GIF apart in the browser: every frame with its delay, rectangle and disposal method, the colour tables, the loop count, any metadata, and a byte-by-byte account of the file size. Nothing is uploaded.

## Documents & audio

Rearrange a document or trim a recording, without sending either off to be processed.

- [PDF Merger & Splitter](https://abox.tools/merge-pdf/): Merge PDFs, split one into several files, and reorder, rotate or remove pages in your browser. Pages are copied between documents locally, so no file is ever uploaded.
- [PDF Compressor](https://abox.tools/compress-pdf/): Compress a PDF in your browser. Images are recompressed against how large they are actually drawn on the page, and the document is rewritten locally, so no file is ever uploaded.
- [Images to PDF](https://abox.tools/images-to-pdf/): Combine JPG, PNG and WebP images into a single PDF document. Every page is written in your browser, so no image is ever uploaded.
- [Audio Trimmer](https://abox.tools/trim-audio/): Mark any number of parts of a recording while it plays, then save those parts as a single file - or cut them out and keep the rest. Cuts land on the exact sample marked, with an optional few-millisecond fade so the joins do not click. Nothing is uploaded and the result is written as a WAV, so nothing is re-encoded.
- [Audio Editor](https://abox.tools/edit-audio/): Reverse an audio track, change its speed with or without moving the pitch, and set its level, in the browser. Works on the audio inside a video too. Nothing is uploaded and the result is written as a WAV, so nothing is re-encoded.

## Text, codes & passwords

Read it, check it, or make it here - no token, no config file and no password on somebody else's server.

- [Text & Code](https://abox.tools/text-tools/): Format and minify JSON, XML, HTML, CSS and YAML, compare two texts with a line and word diff, encode and decode Base64, URLs, HTML entities and hex, and convert JSON to YAML or XML and back. Everything runs in the browser and nothing is uploaded.
- [QR & Barcode Generator](https://abox.tools/qr-barcode/): Generate a QR code or a linear barcode from a string in the browser. QR codes for links, Wi-Fi networks, contact cards, email, SMS, phone numbers and coordinates, with all four error-correction levels; EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, ITF-14, Interleaved 2 of 5, Code 128 and Code 39 barcodes with their check digits. Download as SVG or PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
- [QR & Barcode Reader](https://abox.tools/qr-barcode-reader/): Read a QR code or a linear barcode from an image, a screenshot or a live camera, entirely in the browser. Shows the decoded string and, for links, the host it would reach, before anything is opened. Supports QR versions 1 to 40 with Reed-Solomon error correction, and EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ITF-14, Interleaved 2 of 5, Code 128 and Code 39. Nothing is uploaded and no camera frame is recorded.
- [Hash & Checksum](https://abox.tools/hash-checksum/): Work out the MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 checksum of any file in the browser, and compare it against the value a download page published. The file is read in pieces and never uploaded.
- [Password & Passphrase Generator](https://abox.tools/password-generator/): Generate strong random passwords and diceware passphrases in the browser. Characters are drawn with crypto.getRandomValues and words from a bundled 7,776-word EFF list; the page reports the exact entropy of what it made. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is stored.

## Guides

Written for the person doing the job rather than for the tool: what each setting
means, what it costs, and when not to bother.

- [How to compress an image to an exact file size](https://abox.tools/guides/compress-an-image-to-a-target-size/): An upload form wants 500 KB and your photo is 4 MB. What a size limit really costs, which setting to move first, and why a PNG will not shrink the way a JPEG does.
- [How to resize an image without wrecking it](https://abox.tools/guides/resize-an-image/): What happens to a picture when you change its pixel dimensions: why shrinking is safe and enlarging is not, what to do when the box is the wrong shape, and when to crop instead.
- [How to take a passport photo that is not sent back](https://abox.tools/guides/make-a-passport-photo/): What a passport photo is actually measured on - head height, eye line, background - which country wants which numbers, and how to hit the pixel and KB limits an online form enforces.
- [How to make a favicon that still reads at sixteen pixels](https://abox.tools/guides/make-a-favicon/): Which sizes a favicon.ico actually needs, which extra files iPhones, Android and a Mac ask for, and why a logo that works on a poster disappears at sixteen pixels.
- [How to convert an SVG to a PNG at the right size](https://abox.tools/guides/convert-an-svg-to-png/): A vector has no pixel size of its own, so the number is yours to choose. Where that number comes from for a screen, an app icon and a printer, and what changes when a drawing becomes pixels.
- [When to put a picture inside your CSS, and when not to](https://abox.tools/guides/embed-an-image-in-css/): What a data URI costs, why base64 adds a third and gzip does not give it back, why an SVG should never be base64, and the quoting mistake that breaks inlined SVGs silently.
- [What a photo says about you, and how to take it out](https://abox.tools/guides/remove-exif-and-gps-data/): A photo off a phone usually carries the exact spot it was taken, the time to the second, and the camera's serial number. What is in there, who can read it, and how to take it out without touching the picture.
- [How to redact an image so the hidden part is really gone](https://abox.tools/guides/redact-an-image/): Black boxes drawn in most programs sit on top of the picture and can be moved aside. What separates a real redaction from a covered one, why pixelated text can be read back, and how to check a file before you send it.
- [The photo your phone saved, and the format nothing will open](https://abox.tools/guides/convert-heic-to-jpg/): iPhones save photos as HEIC, and half the internet cannot open one. What the format is, why only Safari decodes it, what converting costs the picture, and how to do it without uploading the photos to anyone.
- [How to merge, split and reorder PDF pages](https://abox.tools/guides/merge-and-split-pdf-files/): Combine PDFs, cut one into several, and move pages around: what survives the reshuffle, what no tool can carry across, and why none of it needs uploading your documents anywhere.
- [How to make a PDF smaller, and why some will not shrink](https://abox.tools/guides/make-a-pdf-smaller/): Where a PDF's size actually is, why a scan compresses 80% and a contract barely moves, what DPI means here, and what a compressor should never do to your document.
- [How to combine images into one PDF](https://abox.tools/guides/combine-images-into-a-pdf/): Turn photos or scans into a single PDF: page size, order and rotation, why a JPEG need not lose any quality on the way in, and what a PDF tells the person you send it to.
- [How to turn a folder of images into a video](https://abox.tools/guides/turn-images-into-a-video/): Make an MP4 slideshow from photos: what frame rate and duration actually control, how to handle pictures that are the wrong shape, and why the result has no soundtrack.
- [How to make an animated GIF from images](https://abox.tools/guides/make-a-gif-from-images/): Turn a set of pictures into one animated GIF: how fast a GIF can really play, what the palette setting changes, and the three things that actually make the file smaller.
- [How to trim a video without re-encoding it](https://abox.tools/guides/trim-a-video/): Cutting a clip need not lose a single byte of quality. Why a cut sometimes lands earlier than you marked it, what a keyframe has to do with it, and when to accept a re-encode.
- [How to crop a video to a different shape](https://abox.tools/guides/crop-a-video/): Cut a clip down to a square, a 9:16 portrait, or an exact pixel box. Which ratio each platform wants, why cropping has to re-encode when trimming does not, and what that costs.
- [How to reverse a video](https://abox.tools/guides/reverse-a-video/): Play a clip backwards: what reversing does to the picture and the sound, why it cannot be done without re-encoding, why it is slower than trimming, and what to do first.
- [How to save a frame from a video as a picture](https://abox.tools/guides/grab-a-frame-from-a-video/): Get a still out of a clip at its real resolution: why a screenshot of a paused player is not the same picture, which format to save it in, and how to land on the exact frame you meant.
- [How to trim audio without losing quality](https://abox.tools/guides/trim-an-audio-file/): Where an audio cut actually lands, why it can be exact when a video cut cannot, why a join sometimes clicks, and what a five-millisecond fade is really doing.
- [How to make a QR code that still scans on somebody else's phone](https://abox.tools/guides/make-a-qr-code/): Which error-correction level to pick, why the white margin around a QR code is part of the code, how big to print it, and what a free generator's 'dynamic' code costs you later.
- [How to check a download against its checksum](https://abox.tools/guides/verify-a-file-checksum/): How to check an MD5 or SHA-256 checksum on Windows, macOS and Linux or in your browser, what a match actually proves, and the mistake that makes the whole exercise pointless.
- [How to turn a video into a GIF](https://abox.tools/guides/turn-a-video-into-a-gif/): Which section, which width and which frame rate to choose, why a GIF of a video is ten times the size of the video, and when to use one at all.
- [How to split a GIF into frames](https://abox.tools/guides/split-a-gif-into-frames/): Get every frame of an animated GIF as a PNG: why some frames are only a small patch of the picture, what happens to the transparency, and how to keep the timing so you can put it back together.
- [What is actually inside a GIF](https://abox.tools/guides/whats-inside-a-gif/): Frames, delays, disposal methods and colour tables explained, why browsers refuse the fastest delays, and how to work out where a GIF's file size really went.
- [How to format JSON without handing it to anybody](https://abox.tools/guides/format-json-without-uploading-it/): How to lay out, check and minify JSON in your own browser - what a formatter must never change about your file, how to read the error message, and why the site you paste it into matters.
- [Is it safe to upload files to online converters?](https://abox.tools/guides/is-it-safe-to-upload-files/): Most online converters send your file to a server. What that means, what happens to it there, and four checks that tell you whether a tool needs to.

## Optional

Background rather than answers. Skip these if you are short of room.

- [All guides](https://abox.tools/guides/): Plain guides to compressing, resizing, cropping, trimming and converting your own files - what the settings mean, what they cost, and why none of it needs an upload.
- [Roadmap](https://abox.tools/roadmap/): Every tool planned for abox.tools, grouped and in the open, plus the ones already finished. All of them run in your browser and upload nothing.
- [github.com/A-Box-of-Tools/website](https://github.com/A-Box-of-Tools/website): Every page and every tool here. One folder per tool, each with a README and its work in dependency-free ES modules under src/. The code is MIT, the prose is CC BY 4.0, and LICENSE at the root sets out which is which.
- [Sitemap](https://abox.tools/sitemap.xml): Every page of every language, with the date each last changed.
- [Privacy & Cookies](https://abox.tools/privacy/): What abox.tools does and does not collect. Your files are never uploaded; the ads, the visit counter and the donate button are each described in full.
- [Terms of Use](https://abox.tools/terms/): The terms this site is offered under: free, as-is, no account, no warranty, and your files remain entirely your own because they are never sent to us.
